transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I need to conduct a round-robin review with lab quality, waste logistics, and warehouse supervision before I can approve the removal plan and shipment controls. Can we get started on that review?

transcript.text: Before we proceed with the authorization, I need to flag something critical. My laboratory analysis on these drums, completed yesterday, found 2.4% chlorinated solvent in the spent coolant. Per our site's waste matrix, any batch at or above 1.0% chlorinated solvent must be routed to hazardous-liquid treatment rather than ordinary coolant recycling. This result has not yet been attached to the waste authorization, so we need to account for it before approving the removal plan and shipment controls.

transcript.text: Before we finalize the shipment controls, I need to flag something on the logistics side. I confirmed with the disposal contractor that their tanker permit allows no more than 8 of these drums on one load, so the 14 drums will need to be shipped as two separate loads — one of 8 and a second of 6. I received this permit condition in the contractor's service email but haven't yet entered it into the transport booking system, so we need to account for it in the removal plan.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag something from my warehouse inspection. I found active seepage at the base of exactly 4 of the 14 drums. Those 4 drums must be placed in UN-rated overpacks before any movement. The other 10 drums are fine on their existing spill pallets. I recorded this on the shift clipboard, but I haven't yet updated the waste file, so we need to account for this in the removal plan.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text:
Thank you all for those critical flags. Let me summarize what we need to account for before I can approve the removal plan and shipment controls:

1. Ravi — Lab analysis found 2.4% chlorinated solvent, which exceeds the 1.0% threshold, so these drums must be routed to hazardous-liquid treatment, not ordinary coolant recycling. That result needs to be attached to the waste authorization.

2. Megan — The contractor's tanker permit limits each load to 8 drums, so we'll need two shipments: 8 drums first, then 6 drums. That permit condition needs to be entered into the transport booking system.

3. Tomas — 4 of the 14 drums have active seepage and must go into UN-rated overpacks before any movement. The other 10 remain on their existing spill pallets. That finding needs to be updated in the waste file.

Based on all three flags, here's what I'm prepared to approve:
- Waste route: hazardous-liquid treatment (per Ravi's lab result)
- All 14 drums authorized for removal
- First load: 8 drums, second load: 6 drums (per Megan's permit condition)
- 4 drums require UN-rated overpacks before movement (per Tomas's inspection)

Before I formally settle the authorization, does anyone have additional concerns or corrections?
